5 Megapixels of Global Conservation

A transparent map of global conservation effort

In 2017, the OECD estimated global biodiversity finance at USD 78-91 billion, while potentially harmful investments reached USD 500 billion. Despite this spending, we lack a comprehensive map of where conservation effort actually happens on the ground.

With Earth's surface at 510 million km², dividing into 100 km² pixels gives us 5.1 million pixels – the resolution of an average digital camera in 2010. We aim to create a transparent map showing conservation patrol coverage for each of these pixels.

This tool monitors 162 African keystone protected areas covering 2.1 million km², tracking fire events, deforestation, settlements, and patrol effort to ensure accountability and reveal where resources are needed most.

Quick Start

  • Click a park to see fire, settlement & deforestation data
  • Use time slider to filter data by date range
  • Upload GPX to add patrol tracks (upload button)
  • Star parks to save and generate reports
  • Bell icon shows fire alerts & notifications

Data Layers

  • Fire Activity – Satellite detections grouped into trajectories with origin/destination
  • Settlements – Built-up areas classified by type and distance to park
  • Deforestation – Forest loss events clustered and classified by cause
  • Patrol Tracks – GPS coverage intensity in 10×10 km grid cells

How We Process Data

Fire Detection (v5)

  • Source: NASA VIIRS satellite (375m resolution, 12-hour revisit)
  • Daily download at 3am UTC from FIRMS NRT API + 30km buffer
  • Fires clustered using DBSCAN (5km radius) into groups
  • Groups tracked across days using 12-hour time windows
  • Trajectories smoothed to eliminate zigzag artifacts
  • Movement direction, speed, and trajectory quality calculated
  • Position classified: stopped inside, transited, entirely outside

Settlement Detection

  • Source: EU Global Human Settlement Layer (10m resolution)
  • Built-up pixels clustered into settlement polygons
  • Distance to park boundary and nearest road calculated
  • Classified: village, farm compound, herding camp, fishing camp, seasonal camp, possible mining site — inferred from river proximity, deforestation shape, fire seasonality and remoteness

Deforestation Analysis

  • Source: Hansen Global Forest Change (30m resolution)
  • Annual tree cover loss 2001-2024
  • Clustered into events (5km radius)
  • Classified: agricultural clearing, logging, charcoal production
  • Near-real-time: GFW integrated alerts (GLAD-S2/RADD, ~10m) with 100km buffer — one park rescanned per day

Patrol Tracking

  • Upload GPX tracks from GPS devices or apps
  • Tracks split into 10×10 km grid cells
  • Movement classified: foot (<7 km/h), vehicle (7-80), aircraft (>80) with subtypes: boat, fixed-wing, rotor-wing from trajectory analysis
  • Intensity = % of 1km subcells visited in each grid cell

Update Schedule

Fire data Daily at 5am CAT
Deforestation alerts (GFW) Daily rotation — one park/day
Park narratives refresh Daily — follows the scanned park
Research papers Daily (OpenAlex API)
Legal documents Weekly (FAOLEX)
Patrol data On upload (instant)

Select a park to view learned features

Connect to external GPS tracking services (e.g. EarthRanger / PAMDAS) to automatically fetch patrol tracks daily. Tracks are anonymised — no names or personal data are stored. Only person, vehicle, and aircraft tracks are fetched; animal collar data is excluded.

Credential security
Passwords are encrypted with AES-256-GCM before storage — they are never saved in plaintext and never passed as command-line arguments. The encryption key is stored separately with restricted file permissions. Disabling a source immediately purges its stored password.

Share links

The short links this login has issued. Other logins keep their own list.

named link
a short name for a view — it still asks for the password, so the name is safe to say out loud.
shared key
opens the view without a password: read-only, expires by itself; Switch off revokes it for whoever holds it.
#tag
groups links made for one purpose (e.g. a report) so they renew together. A link can carry several. Click a name to rename it on every link that has it, × to take this link out.

Shared files

Upload a file (a styled GeoPackage, a PDF…) and hand it out with an expiring key. The file lives 21 days by default and is kept as long as any live key points at it — a 90-day key keeps the file 90 days. When the last key dies, the file is swept.

Loading…

Areas of interest & ingest

Areas of interest visible to this login, their owners, and what each dataset's ingest queue is doing. Passwords are never shown — a principal is identified by a non-secret sha256 handle. Disabling a dataset keeps its cursor, so re-enabling resumes rather than re-spending API quota.

Principals

Background Map

Choose the basemap style for the globe view. Satellite imagery provides high-resolution aerial photos, useful for detailed analysis.

Historical Maps

Drape a scanned survey series over the current basemap. On screen the ink is inverted to white so the imagery underneath stays readable; the download keeps the original black ink, which is what offline viewers with light backgrounds need.

Checking for installed archives…

Geology

Scanned regional geological maps, vectorized into one layer: every unit is a polygon, coloured by age (ICS/CGMW chart) and patterned by rock type (FGDC-STD-013-2006), so two sheets printed 40 years apart read as one map. Filter by rock type or by what a rock type can host; how it is drawn (printed ink instead of age, ornament off, individual units) is under Advanced. Commodity groupings are an inference from lithology — “rocks of this kind host gold” — and are not a record of any deposit.
